answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because juniper only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, relic is enforced in the ledger: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any delta approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
